preconditions.expression: len(stdin.split()) == 1 + int(stdin.split()[0]) and all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**9 for x in stdin.split()[1:])
preconditions.description: The first line contains an integer k = 4^n (1 ≤ k ≤ 2·10^6), and the second line contains exactly k integers a_i (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^9).
The input size k must be a power of 4 (i.e., k = 4^n for some non-negative integer n).

postconditions.description: The output is the maximum possible beauty of the matrix, where beauty is computed recursively as follows: for a 2^n × 2^n matrix, the beauty is the maximum element in the matrix plus the sum of the beauties of its four 2^{n-1} × 2^{n-1} submatrices (if n > 0). If n = 0, the beauty is the single element in the matrix.

postconditions.expression: max_possible_beauty(stdin) == max(m + sum(max_possible_beauty(submatrix) for submatrix in split_matrix(matrix, n)), for matrix in all_permutations(stdin.split()[1:], 2**n, 2**n))
postconditions.description: The maximum beauty is obtained by optimally arranging the input numbers into a 2^n × 2^n matrix such that the recursive beauty formula is maximized. The beauty is computed as the maximum element in the matrix plus the sum of the beauties of its four quadrants (recursively).
